audit_findings: Climb production had module implementations for Butler-Volmer exchange and l-squared-over-D transport, but the simulator used three independent plain Arrhenius rates.
Serial stage changes within one PF step reused the entry-stage rate instead of each stage's distinct rate.
Packet-reset multihit behavior had encounter reset semantics but no finite renewal duration.
Intermediate stochastic hits and serial stage transitions were absent from the event ledger.
corrections: Production exchange rate is absolute Butler-Volmer flux divided by release quota.
Production transport rate is the reciprocal of C times domain-length-squared over diffusivity.
Serial stages consume residual timestep using their own rates and write each transition.
Packet renewal duration is explicit and checkpointed; every stochastic hit is ledgered.
Activation analysis counts primitive stochastic events without duplicate release-summary rows.
policy: All partial checkpoints, event ledgers, and trajectories remain in place. They are excluded from final inference, and the full 165-run matrix is relaunched from the corrected tested SHA.
